title: TCU auditors identify overlapping BR-153 maintenance tenders after receiving an Alice email
summary: Alice, the federal audit court's tender-reading robot, emailed tender information to auditors, who found road-maintenance notices that overlapped a concession; the court ordered them annulled.
account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice and auction record published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It had been running for about ten months when the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) presented it at a joint data-analysis seminar of the TCU and the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) on 25–26 September 2017. Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found that DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. A JOTA article of 22 November 2017 states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. The two sources give different numbers of notices and amounts. The court’s site does not expose the complete acórdão. The decision date is not reported. A firsthand report of a July 2018 visit to TCU states that Alice’s email contained no irregularity alert. It states that auditors identified the concession overlap after receiving the information. It reproduces the order to annul notices 88/2017 and 102/2017, and it describes their combined value as R$39 million. The operative part of Acórdão 1.116/2017-Plenário, reproduced in the visit report, gave DNIT's Goiás and Federal District unit fifteen days to annul pregões 88/2017-12 and 102/2017-12. Fernanda Odilla (Crime, Law and Social Change, 2023) reports, citing an interviewee, that TCU added a random forest classifier to the rules that CGU first wrote for Alice. She lists alert overflow and false positives among the main weaknesses of the procurement tools that include Alice.
purpose: Daily automated screening of federal tender notices for signs of irregularity so that auditors can act during the public phase of a tender. This use was its intended purpose.
system: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais), TCU/CGU text-analysis and data cross-checking robot
developer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) with the Ministério da Transparência e Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), in-house
deployer: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), Goiás unit
domain: Public administration: external audit and procurement control
segment: Federal court of accounts (anti-waste and anti-corruption control)

The outcome is material to DNIT and TCU. Inforchannel and JOTA report that an acórdão blocked or canceled the tenders, and the July 2018 visit report reproduces the order to annul notices 88/2017 and 102/2017. Inforchannel gives R$39 million for two notices, and JOTA gives R$20 million for one.
A single highway tender among some 60,000 federal tenders a year, small at national scale.

fields.summary: Alice, the federal audit court's tender-reading robot, emailed tender information to auditors, who found road-maintenance notices that overlapped a concession; the court ordered them annulled.
fields.account: Alice (Análise de Licitações e Editais) is the Tribunal de Contas da União's robot. It reads every tender notice and auction record published on Comprasnet and the Diário Oficial da União. It had been running for about ten months when the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) presented it at a joint data-analysis seminar of the TCU and the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU) on 25–26 September 2017. Inforchannel (27 September 2017), quoting TCU auditor Valéria Nakano, reported that in Goiás the court, via Alice, found that DNIT's state unit had published two notices. They were worth R$39 million for maintenance of the BR-153 on stretches under concession, where maintenance falls to the concessionaire. Within two months an acórdão blocked both tenders. A JOTA article of 22 November 2017 states that Alice was decisive in Acórdão-TCU 1.116/2017 (rapporteur Minister Walton Alencar Rodrigues). It ordered cancellation of the BR-153 tender budgeted at R$20 million. The two sources give different numbers of notices and amounts. The court’s site does not expose the complete acórdão. The decision date is not reported. A firsthand report of a July 2018 visit to TCU states that Alice’s email contained no irregularity alert. It states that auditors identified the concession overlap after receiving the information. It reproduces the order to annul notices 88/2017 and 102/2017, and it describes their combined value as R$39 million. The operative part of Acórdão 1.116/2017-Plenário, reproduced in the visit report, gave DNIT's Goiás and Federal District unit fifteen days to annul pregões 88/2017-12 and 102/2017-12. Fernanda Odilla (Crime, Law and Social Change, 2023) reports, citing an interviewee, that TCU added a random forest classifier to the rules that CGU first wrote for Alice. She lists alert overflow and false positives among the main weaknesses of the procurement tools that include Alice.

value.text: Auditors identified the problem, and the court ordered the tenders annulled.

provenance.basis: A firsthand report of a TCU visit says that Alice sent an email without an irregularity alert; auditors then identified the concession issue. The court’s current search interface did not expose the ruling. The visit report reproduces the cancellation provisions and reports the auditors’ explanation. Auditor visit report, pages 9–11, including reproduced ruling provisions.
